newsitem.title: GERMANY: Feminist Hite takes sex to info superhighway.
newsitem.headline: Feminist Hite takes sex to info superhighway.

text.p: Controversial feminist Shere Hite took to the information superhighway on Friday to spell out what she knows about sex in a frank and freewheeling format.
Bridling at suggestions she was an electronic agony aunt, she said: "I am not a counsellor. I would like to provide the fruits of the knowledge I have acquired over the years."
So Hite, famed for her frank reports that blame men for much of women's sexual frustrations, sat down at the world's largest book fair for an on-line session with whoever tuned in.
The first results were somewhat chaotic as subscribers kept interrupting on screen with a flow of questions that overwrote what she said.
But they soon stopped chipping in when one caller asked how to bring a woman to orgasm by hand and the author of four famous reports on sexuality replied with some graphic and detailed suggestions.
However the formula is to be more structured in future for the service she is providing for the German electronic publisher Bsmedic on America On Line (AOL)

"I will provide an 800-word essay every month on a theme like infidelity, clitoral stimulation or violence in sex. People will ask questions about the theme and that is when the dialogue will happen," she explained.

"It is useful. Some people will get a lot out of it. Some will trivialise it, those who cannot help tittering when sex is mentioned," she told Reuters at the fair which has attracted more than 9,000 publishers from 110 countries.
Hite, vilified by the U.S. media and sociologists for her controversial reports on sexuality, has renounced her American citizenship and acquired a German passport.
She is married to German concert pianist Friedrich Hoericke and has ambitions to further the feminist cause by standing for the European parliament.
The Frankfurt book fair, which has put much of the accent this year on the electronic media, clearly offers another major challenge that appeals to Hite after years under fire.

She looks on her new electronic contract as a health service. "I don't like the word advice. Coming up through the women's movement, I sort of feel we have had enough advice. This is an interactive kind of thing."
